take.en: An agent writes React. raea renders that file on your GPU into a film, a 3D scene, or a small game.

why.en: Product films still leave the codebase. A coding agent can write the frames, but most render paths are a browser timeline or a cloud editor. raea keeps the render on the machine you already have, and the agent can pull one frame, look at it, and fix it before you watch.

explanation.en: raea is a local render engine for video, motion, 3D, and games. You describe the piece. Your agent writes a React and TypeScript composition. A Rust runtime built on Bevy draws it on your GPU and writes an MP4. The same file can play live as a game or open as a scene you walk through. The desktop app holds the chat, the feed, and a timeline you can trim by hand. The current release is 0.1.8.

howItWorks.en: Install the CLI from raea.io. It adds skills so Claude Code knows how to write and check a composition. Ask for the film. The agent writes the file, runs raea render, and can save one frame as a PNG to inspect. raea check flags clipped text, weak contrast, and loudness before export. raea play runs the file live. raea export-game turns a game into its own program.

different.en: HyperFrames turns HTML into a deterministic MP4 in a browser. raea draws on the GPU through Bevy, so one composition can be a film, a walkable scene, or a game. The license is Functional Source License 1.1. Use it and change it. Do not ship a hosted product that replaces raea. Each version becomes Apache-2.0 two years after release.
